messages:
alex: Rolling v2.1.3 to canary (30%) now. quick smoke looked good before canary, tagging @rachel for observability checks
ops-bot: deploy-started: v2.1.3 -> canary (30%) by alex
rachel: seeing a spike in backend_errors.count on canary nodes, not in prod nodes yet. small #s but p50 error rate up ~0.8% -> 3% over baseline. link: https://observability/redwood/queries?q=backend_errors%20by%20pool
sre-tyler: can you paste the query/result? I only see synthetic success from primary region
rachel: pasted output (short snippet):
```
avg_over_time(backend_errors{pool="canary"}[5m]) = 0.03
avg_over_time(backend_errors{pool="prod"}[5m]) = 0.001
```
maya: are these 5xx from the new handler change in v2.1.3? dev reported a retry edge-case last week
alex: correct, change to request fanout. devs thought retries were bounded. rolling back to 0% is an option but want to confirm impact first
product-eng: customers on canary routes? this is internal traffic split, only a handful of traffic-shaping customers on the preview path. but if FF stays open, downstream routing may expand soon due to autoscale
rachel: also: dashboards for the new handler metric (handler.request_errors) were not added to the canary alerting group — missed in the rollout template. so alerting didn't trigger an explicit pager earlier, only noisy downstream infra alerts started surfacing
oncall-bot: page-created: INCIDENT-2392123456 assigned to oncall (notify: #incidents) 
sre-tyler: ok we're paged. first action: can we flip the feature flag for request-fanout to off for canary? alex can you run kill switch?
alex: running kill now: `/ff toggle request-fanout canary off`
ops-bot: feature-flag: request-fanout - canary -> OFF (executed by alex at 13:47 UTC)
rachel: metrics starting to drop for handler.request_errors, but keep an eye on latency — retries caused backpressure earlier
product-eng: quick customer impact note: only ~4200 preview requests in the last hour, majority internal. low exposure but could escalate if autoscaler increases split. recommend rollback of canary until we patch retry bounds
sre-tyler: agree. two parallel mitigations: 1) keep FF off and monitor for 15m; 2) if any symptom appears in prod traffic (which could happen if routing rule expands), prepare canary rollback to previous image and re-run postmortem checks
maya: devs ran a narrow repro. root cause seems to be an unbounded retry on 502 path resulting in amplified errors under limited load. patch incoming, ETA ~45m
alex: starting canary -> 0% (full stop) to be safe. command: `/deploy scale canary 0% --reason "safety: retry amplification"`
ops-bot: deploy-update: canary scaled to 0% by alex
rachel: alert noise was part of the problem — the alerting policy we depend on fires on aggregate infra symptoms and was swamping the signal we needed (handler-level metric missing from group). submitting follow-up ticket to add handler.request_errors to canary alert group: https://tickets/redwood/INC-7843
sre-tyler: good. for handoff: i'll own incident until patch is in and we get stable metrics for 30m post-patch. @maya please update when patch merged and when canary re-enable decision is made
maya: will post updates. dev will open a change with the fix + regression test for retry gating
product-eng: customer comms: none required now — low exposure. will prepare a proactive note in case we re-enable canary and any preview users see errors
alex: logging timeline and actions in incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/2392123456. tagging for postmortem: observability gap + release checklist missing dashboard + FF kill decision flow
oncall-bot: incident-updated: status -> mitigated (FF off, canary scaled 0%). owner: sre-tyler
sre-tyler: handing off to next oncall in 40m. next_oncall: james. james if you see this, i'll DM transfer and leave runbook in the doc
james: ack will take over at 14:30 UTC. please include contact for dev lead in runbook
sre-tyler: added dev lead contact and current metric screenshots to the incident doc. closing active pager but keeping thread open for follow-ups
product-eng: postmortem items: 1) release checklist enforce adding new handler metrics to canary alerts; 2) add a pre-roll smoke that toggles FF in canary and validates handler metrics; 3) improve FF runbook to include immediate kill then introspect flow (avoid ambiguous partial alerts)
maya: patch PR opened: https://git.redwood/pr/4567 - awaiting review. once merged i'll run canary smoke and ping this thread
alex: thanks everyone. leaving notes in the deploy log and will not re-enable until explicit green from @sre-tyler and @maya
product-eng: closing note: this is a near-miss on customer impact but good catch. postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 09:00 UTC
